component.name: StreamKeep
component.summary: Download VODs, live streams, podcasts, and direct media URLs

description.p: StreamKeep is a multi-platform desktop tool for downloading and archiving live streams, VODs, podcasts, and direct media URLs. Features native extractors for Kick, Twitch, Rumble, SoundCloud, Reddit, Audius, and Podcast RSS feeds, with yt-dlp as a universal fallback.

Includes channel monitoring with auto-recording, download queue with bandwidth scheduling, embedded media player, and post-processing (convert, trim, silence removal, transcription). Experimental: upload destinations (S3, FTP, WebDAV) and a plugin SDK for community extensions are present but not yet reachable from a supported workflow.
Internal work only: the download-queue and executor-lease code now lives in its own module instead of the database monolith, which is down to 4,013 lines from 6,737. No behaviour changes.

A recording can now belong to as many collections as you like while still existing once on disk. Membership is explicit and ordered, and adding a recording to one collection never removes it from another. On export the season layout stays the single real file and each collection gets an additional entry pointing at those same bytes - a hardlink where the filesystem allows one, otherwise a .strm pointer that Plex, Jellyfin, Emby and Kodi all follow. Copying is never a fallback, and the export states which strategy every home used. Manage collections from the command line with "collections list", "add", "remove" and friends.

Your custom site definitions now travel with a backup, arriving inert: a restore strips the per-adapter approvals so each one is review-required on the machine it lands on. Plugins are still never restored, and the restore report now says so rather than leaving their absence to be discovered. Deleted-VOD recovery reports what every candidate CDN domain said instead of just failing, and refuses outright when the platform is gating a VOD rather than probing around the control. Internally the browser companion's security boundary, host and origin validation, and remote-UI rendering all became modules that own their own code.

The yt-dlp update channel is now a setting: StreamKeep still ships a frozen, version-checked build by default, but you can point it at your own to follow nightly, and a build below the supported floor is refused by name rather than trusted. The health panel reports which channel is actually in use, not the one requested. An intermittent crash at the end of a test run was traced to a background health probe still running when the window that owned it went away; stopping such a probe no longer requires killing the thread it runs on.

Channel backfill now fetches whatever is closest to being deleted rather than whatever is newest, so a long queue no longer loses the oldest reachable replay on platforms that delete their own VODs, and the queue row says why each item was ordered where it is. Internally the database decomposition continued: the history action log, the tombstone ledger and published-recording identifiers now live in modules that own them.

The language selector now states how much of each catalog is actually translated and marks incomplete ones as beta, so switching to a partly-translated language no longer produces a mostly-English interface with no explanation. Internally, the database schema module now owns the migrations it had only been dispatching, and the history action log became a module of its own.

A live capture ended by a crash or a power loss now leaves a playable recording instead of an unreadable file, and the final repack can no longer cost the capture it was meant to tidy up. Bulk archiving backs off on its own when a host throttles, per host, so one strict site no longer slows the rest of the queue. The database split began actually moving behaviour out of its legacy module rather than forwarding it.

AI-upscaled video is no longer selectable by accident, so an archive keeps the real rendition rather than a synthesised one that merely reports a taller resolution. A platform whose extractor keeps failing now raises a health condition naming the platform and the engine that failed, and its engine can be switched for that platform alone. An adapter edit that leaves the file the same size is no longer missed, and the intermittent native crash at the end of a test run is fixed.

StreamKeep now takes an explicit position on FFmpeg 9.0: support is decided on the reported libavcodec ABI major rather than a version string, an untested ABI is refused by name instead of accepted silently, and certificate verification for remote inputs is stated explicitly so 8.x and 9.0 behave identically.

Declarative source adapters now stay inert until their outbound request contract is reviewed and approved, from the desktop or the CLI. Translation providers are routed through the guarded transport with bounded responses, window close joins every worker it owns, backups carry per-source download archives, browser cookie imports report why they failed, and a restored library reconciles its semantic index.

Gallery-dl image sets can now be ingested into the local library with public metadata, optional CBZ or ZIP packaging, and safe cover rendering; local semantic search and opt-in metadata translation also ship in this release.

Failed downloads now retry themselves on transient errors and survive a restart; credentials become named profiles bound to the sites they may authenticate; automatic rotating backups are schedulable and observable; live captures report dropped fragments and preserve raw footage for salvage; and audio downloads get their album-artist filled in. Windows now ships as a fast-starting directory install with an unsigned installer instead of a 520 MB single file.

Audit fixes: fetching a video URL that carries a playlist parameter now resolves the requested video instead of failing or picking another entry; playlist URLs get an actionable hint instead of a slow failure; a stopped live recording no longer offers a bogus resume next launch; command-line output no longer garbles or drops lines with special characters.
Fixes the fetch appearing stuck on "fetching stream info" for a former-livestream YouTube VOD: resolving these now takes a second or two instead of about two minutes.
Fixes being unable to download a former-livestream YouTube VOD: these take longer to resolve than the old 60-second limit allowed, so the resolve timeout is now larger and configurable.
Fixes a crash ("no attribute adv_override_badge") that aborted every download when you pressed Download selected.
Fixes a bug where a live stream captured while in progress (YouTube and any yt-dlp source) was deleted when you pressed Stop. Stopping a live recording now keeps the footage captured so far.

Adds two optional external download engines: gallery-dl for image galleries and social-media posts (Twitter/X, Instagram, Pixiv, boorus), and lux for Chinese platforms (Bilibili, Douyin, Youku), each exposed as a CLI subcommand that shares the configured output folder, cookies, and proxy.

Wires the storage-health disk monitor with auto-pause and native OS notifications into notable events, adds guided YouTube PO-token/SABR remediation, enforces an SSRF address policy on the REST server, and defers subscribed YouTube downloads so SponsorBlock segments can aggregate.

Adds a Packagizer-class ordered rules engine, keep-last-N per-source retention, and a published OpenAPI 3.1 spec for the REST server, plus dedicated test coverage for the monitor, chat readers, and finalize pipeline.
Aligns the responsive desktop with the production mockup, fixes cross-thread startup logging, and introduces a unified StreamKeep icon across Windows, Flatpak, the README, and the browser companion.

Refines the complete desktop visual hierarchy, consolidates Download actions into a compact command surface, adds live theme, density, accent, and Spanish controls, and introduces dry-run-first archive maintenance.

Adds aria2c external-downloader routing with URL sanitization, HAR-capture media/manifest import, an optional queue-complete power action, and a streamkeep:// protocol handler with browser bookmarklet.
Makes HLS parsing and resume standards-complete, corrects WebVTT/podcast transcript parsing, and adds bilingual subtitle merge, LRC export, and YouTube live-chat replay normalization.
Adds a non-DRM HLS clear-key override and hardens backup restore, event hooks, remote image handling, plugin isolation, and credential storage.
Adds full yt-dlp output, subtitle, SponsorBlock, and incremental playlist sync controls.
Adds a restart-persistent failed-job recovery ledger with desktop and web-remote retry/discard actions.
Adds archive integrity manifests and History verify/rescan recovery actions.
Security hardening, extractor fixes, and engineering audit.
